statements: If z_i-z_j <= G for every other visible key j, p_i <= 1/(1+(N-1)*exp(-G)).
If every visible score has absolute value <= B, p_i <= 1/(1+(N-1)*exp(-2*B)).
For actual finite-epsilon Q/K RMS and arbitrary rotary phases, m>=0 and any fixed real gain g: p_i <= 1/(1+(N-1)*exp(-2*m*log(N)*abs(g)*d)).
For head width4, m=1/4 and g=1/2, every key has p_i <= N/(2*N-1). The checked N=64 example gives64/127.
hypotheses: Real arithmetic; a nonempty finite row of visible keys.
For normalized attention: positive integer head width d, epsilon>0 and m>=0.
No assumed winning gap; query/key inputs and rotary phases are arbitrary.
The general theorem accepts the actual rounded fixed gain as a real scalar. The width-four specialization explicitly requires gain1/2.
nonvacuity: Every statement has a concrete example. Unequal two-key logits test the first two; normalized examples use actual FP32epsilon1/8388608, varying nonzero phases, widths8and4, and4or64visible keys.
mapping: Reviewed equation correspondence to the projected Q/K RMS, rotary, fixed score gain and visible-key log factor. Not a formal translation of PyTorch.
scope: A probability ceiling for one softmax attention row. It does not bound XSA/readout amplification or prove that a full transformer cannot learn a task. Width4is outside the current fixed benchmark; no long result motivates or tunes this proof. No new model or training arm.
preservation: Supplemental real-arithmetic analysis. Existing scientific sources, configurations, plans, selection and original proof records are unchanged.
